text: This is an axiom which never fails: that a prince who is not wise himself will never take good advice, unless by chance he has yielded his affairs entirely to one person who happens to be a very prudent man. In this case indeed he may be well governed, but it would not be for long, because such a governor would in a short time take away his state from him.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XXIII, How flatterers should be avoided
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
